observations.fact: The SEC-hosted fiscal-2026 operating disclosure reports revenue of $4.6411 billion, up 35.7% from $3.4193 billion in fiscal 2025, with the increase primarily attributed to higher demand for data-center and communications-infrastructure products.
observations.whyItMatters: Gives Alpha source-addressed primary regulatory evidence for financialOperatingMomentum and thesisQuality rather than relying only on issuer press releases.

observations.fact: The same filing reports data-center product revenue of $2.2251 billion, 47.9% of fiscal-2026 revenue, up $645.2 million or 40.8% year over year.
observations.whyItMatters: Quantifies the materiality and growth of the data-center exposure that the existing packet describes qualitatively, while also making concentration/cycle sensitivity measurable for risk and data-confidence work.

risks: Nearly half of reported fiscal-2026 revenue was tied to data-center products, increasing sensitivity to data-center customer demand and capex cycles.
Revenue growth alone does not establish normalized post-acquisition margins, customer concentration, pricing power or valuation.
unknowns: Customer-level concentration inside the data-center segment remains unquantified by this source.
Normalized margin and free-cash-flow conversion of the combined business remain Alpha underwriting questions.
This evidence does not itself establish a numeric Earth score.

confidence.basis: Primary SEC-hosted quantitative operating data directly address the scale and growth of the data-center exposure and materially strengthen source-addressed underwriting inputs.
